sections.heading: Overview
content: The following policy outlines Humana’s billing requirements and reimbursement for claims for healthcare services provided due to automobile and workplace injuries.

sections.heading: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicare Advantage (MA) plans allow claims for healthcare services provided due to automobile and workplace injuries according to applicable Medicare Secondary Payer (MSP) guidelines. A provider must make all reasonable efforts to determine whether there is other coverage for an automobile or workplace injury, such as under automobile or workers’ compensation insurance, and must promptly report as described below, in claims submitted to Humana, and any such other coverage that is identified. Additionally, a provider must bill a patient’s automobile or workplace injury insurance plan, if applicable, before billing the patient’s Humana MA plan. Finally, a provider must promptly forward to Humana any determination by an automobile or workplace insurance plan made with respect to a claim for a Humana MA enrollee’s injuries. A provider’s failure to promptly fulfill any requirement could affect Humana’s disposition of a claim after initial receipt and/or after initial adjudication. Humana expects providers to abide by the MSP billing requirements when submitting claims to Humana MA plans. If a provider identifies automobile insurance, the provider must include the information below when submitting a paper claim to Humana, or equivalent information when submitting an electronic claim to Humana. For a CMS-1500 form or its electronic equivalent: • Enter “yes” in box 10-B • Enter the accident date in field 14 • Enter all diagnosis codes in section 21 • Attach the following to the claim, if available: – Copy of the check from the primary insurance carrier – Copy of the explanation of benefits (EOB) from the primary insurance carrier – Copy of the exhaustion denial letter from the primary insurance carrier – Personal injury protection (PIP) worksheet, if available – Statement from the patient indicating no PIP coverage, if applicable For a UB-04 form or its electronic equivalent: • Enter occurrence code 01 or 02, as applicable, and the accident date in fields 33 – 35 • Enter value code 14 in fields 39 – 41 • Enter all diagnosis codes in fields 67 – 76 • Attach the following to the claim, if available: – Copy of the check from the primary insurance carrier – Copy of the EOB from the primary insurance carrier – Copy of the exhaustion denial letter from the primary insurance carrier – Statement from the patient indicating no PIP coverage, if applicable If a provider identifies workers’ compensation insurance, the provider must include the information below when submitting a paper claim to Humana, or equivalent information when submitting an electronic claim to Humana. For a CMS-1500 form or its electronic equivalent: • Enter “yes” in box 10-B • Enter the accident date in field 14 • Enter all diagnosis codes in section 21 • Attach the following to the claim, if available: – Copy of the check from the primary insurance carrier – Copy of the EOB from the primary insurance carrier – Copy of the exhaustion denial letter from the primary insurance carrier – Statement from the patient confirming that their employer does not provide workers’ compensation coverage For a UB-04 form or its electronic equivalent: • Enter occurrence code 04 and accident date in fields 33 – 35 • Enter condition code 02, 05, or 77, as applicable, in fields 18 – 28 • Enter value code 15 or 41, as applicable, in fields 39 – 41 • Enter all diagnosis codes in fields 67 – 76 • Attach the following to the claim, if available: – Copy of the check from the primary insurance carrier – Copy of the EOB from the primary insurance carrier – Copy of the exhaustion denial letter from the primary insurance carrier – Statement from the patient confirming that their employer does not provide workers’ compensation coverage Note: Medicare benefits are secondary regardless of whether the patient wishes to file a workers’ compensation claim. Humana may deny a claim for healthcare services provided due to an automobile or workplace injury if it is submitted without the information above. Humana may deny a claim when payment has been made, or when payment may reasonably be expected to be made, under any applicable liability insurance arrangement, including self-insurance, no-fault insurance or workers’ compensation law or plan. Humana may also require providers to pursue and exhaust available no-fault insurance or workers’ compensation coverage and to demonstrate reasonable efforts to exhaust any other applicable coverage, before submitting claims to Humana for payment. Note: For more guidance on the MSP provisions and billing requirements, see the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services’ MSP booklet and the MSP manual in the References section of this policy.

sections.heading: Medicaid Payment Policy
content: In addition to the policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. Humana Medicaid plans allow claims for healthcare services provided due to automobile and workplace injuries according to applicable state Medicaid agency requirements.

sections.heading: General Humana Resources
content: • Availity – Providers can register for access to information on a variety of topics such as eligibility, benefits, referrals, authorizations, claims and electronic remittances. • Claims processing edit notifications – Alerts of upcoming claims payment changes are posted on the first Friday of each month. • Claims resources – Providers can find information on referrals, authorizations, electronic claim submissions and more. • Making it easier – This page contains an educational series for providers and healthcare professionals. • Medical and pharmacy coverage policies – Humana publishes determinations of coverage of medical procedures, devices and medications for the treatment of various conditions. There may be variances in coverage among plans. • Publications – This page can help you find our quarterly newsletter, provider manual and other resources to help you do business with us. Note : Links to sources outside of Humana’s control are verified at the time of publication. Please report broken links .
